findings.title: Prisma.Sql deep equality fails for reduce-built conditions
findings.body: These expectations compare a whole Prisma.Sql object with a flat template, but the service builds team/org/filter combinations with nested Prisma.sql calls and reduce. Prisma.Sql equality is structural over its strings and values arrays; nested composition leaves different string segmentation even when the SQL text is identical. For example, the service OR condition has five strings while this flat template has three. Therefore the team, org, and combined-filter assertions at lines 296, 332, and 429 will fail. Compare conditions.sql/text plus values instead, or build the expected SQL with the same nested structure.

findings.title: getBaseConditions can return an unparenthesized OR expression
findings.body: When there is no filter, getBaseConditions returns the authorization expression directly. For org/team scopes that expression is an unparenthesized top-level OR, e.g. (A) OR (B). Any caller that composes it as WHERE ${baseConditions} AND ... gets SQL precedence A OR (B AND ...), so the extra predicate is applied only to one branch. This can return rows outside the requested date/status/team range. The returned expression should always be wrapped in parentheses, or callers should use a service method that composes safely.

findings.title: Public findMany API removed without caller migration
findings.body: The public findMany method is removed and replaced by getBaseConditions, which only returns a SQL fragment. No caller updates are included in this PR. Any existing consumer of service.findMany(...) will fail to compile or run, and responsibility for applying authorization moves to every raw-query caller; forgetting to interpolate getBaseConditions would query all rows. Keep a query method that applies the conditions, or migrate all callers in the same PR.

findings.title: Team scope no longer requires teamId at compile time
findings.body: The new public options type makes teamId optional for every scope, whereas the old constructor type was a discriminated union that required teamId for scope "team". Missing teamId now passes TypeScript, fails the runtime schema, and is silently converted to this.options = null, so the service returns 1=0 (empty results) instead of reporting a configuration error. Retain the discriminated union or throw on validation failure.
